files.title: CC151 4 Cultural Activities Tranining and Participation in Performing Arts (For sem II)

subjects.title: Cultural Activities: Training and Participation in Performing Arts Events and Competitions (Drawing, Painting, Sculpture, Music, Dance, Theatre, etc.)

units.title: Suggested Activities
units.topics: 1. Enrolment in at least one performing or visual art activity (college-based or external). 2. Attendance and reflective report on one live or recorded performing arts event. 3. Skill-training log (minimum 20–30 hours) with weekly reflections. 4. Preparation and presentation of a short performance / artwork. 5. Group collaboration assignment (ensemble performance / group artwork). 6. Documentation of rehearsal or creative process (written/visual). 7. Interview with an artist or art educator. 8. Participation in a college or intercollegiate cultural event. 9. Critical appreciation of an art form different from the student’s chosen activity. 10. Portfolio submission (photos, videos, sketches, or recordings). 11. Self-assessment report on learning outcomes (optional).

files.title: CC151 5 PRAYAS Promoting Road Awareness for Youth and Safety (For any semester)

subjects.title: Promoting Road Awareness for Youth and Safety (PRAYAS)

units.title: Traffic Rules & Signs
units.topics: Video lessons (road signs, speed, pedestrian safety), Webinar: “Why Rules Save Lives” (Traffic Police official), Case studies (Pune accidents, PDF + discussion), Seminar + Quiz.

units.title: Licence & Legal Awareness
units.topics: Video lessons (Licence process, penalties, insurance, PUC), Mock RTO test (via LMS, interactive quiz), Webinar: “Legal rights & responsibilities of drivers” (RTO official), Seminar Q&A.

units.title: Helmets, Safety Gear & First Aid
units.topics: Demo videos (Helmet, ISI mark, seatbelts, reflective jackets), Seminar (hands-on demos in college), Practical mock drill (accident response, CPR intro), Webinar: “Golden Hour & First Aid Awareness” (doctor/NGO), Quiz & safety gear checklist.

units.title: Balancing, Vehicle Maintenance & Eco-Driving
units.topics: Video tutorials (daily checks, fuel efficiency, eco-driving), Practical balancing drills (two-wheeler, supervised), Seminar (four-wheeler maintenance basics), Webinar: “Smart Driving = Safe Driving”, Quiz.

units.title: Pollution Control & Green Mobility
units.topics: Video: PUC importance, horn & silencer issues, Seminar: Green Mobility (EV awareness, eco-driving), Webinar with MPCB expert, Activity: On-campus PUC & anti-honking drive, Quiz.

units.title: New–Age Driver Training
units.topics: Simulator-based training (or digital driving modules), Webinar: “EVs & Future of Mobility”, Telematics/navigation tools (app-based learning), Seminar Q&A, Quiz.

units.title: Driving Behaviour & Road Safety
units.topics: Video: behaviour risks (speeding, distraction, substance), Webinar: “Psychology of Safe Driving” (behavioural expert), Seminar: road rage, emotional control, respect on roads, Group discussion (student role plays), Final quiz & feedback.

files.title: CC151 6 Study of Contemporary Issues and News Clippings (For any semester)

subjects.title: Study of Contemporary Issues and News Clippings

units.title: CC Activities
units.topics: 1. Understand the importance of contemporary issues and their role in personal and social life. 2. List the information sources available at home, college and neighborhood. 3. Map the significant contemporary issues at local, regional, national and global level. 4. Shortlist the contemporary issues during present semester and select topic. 5. Register topic with faculty in-charge. 6. Read daily newspapers and magazines; mark and document relevant news stories, editorials, analytical articles. 7. Follow news portals and websites, download relevant material with links. 8. Read relevant books on topic for background knowledge. 9. Interview subject experts if possible. 10. Write an article about topic in 2000 or more words. 11. Study and compare media coverage. 12. Prepare PowerPoint Presentation and present. 13. Submit file of news clippings, written note, PPT.

subjects.title: NSS (Theory & Practice) – II (National Integration, Environment & Social Development)

units.title: National Integration and Environmental Awareness (Theory)
units.topics: 1. National Integration: Meaning, Importance, and Challenges 2. Unity in Diversity and Constitutional Values 3. Environmental Issues: Climate Change, Pollution, Biodiversity 4. Sustainable Development and Role of Youth

units.title: Social Service and Environmental Activities (Practical)
units.topics: 1. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, Plastic-Free Campaigns 2. Tree Plantation, Water Conservation, Cleanliness Drives 3. Awareness programmes on social issues (addiction, gender equality, road safety) 4. Participation in government and NGO-led social initiatives

files.title: CC201 4 Integrated Personality Development Programme I (For Sem III)

subjects.title: Integrated Personality Development Program I

units.title: The Need for Values
units.topics: Students will learn about the need for values as part of their holistic development to become successful in their many roles - as ambitious students, reliable employees, caring family members, and considerate citizens.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Restructuring Yourself
units.topics: Students learn how self-improvement enables them to secure a bright future for themselves. They will learn 6 powerful thought-processes that can develop their intellectual, physical, emotional, and spiritual quotients.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Power of Habit
units.topics: Students will undergo a study of how habits work, the habits of successful professionals, and the practical techniques that can be used to develop good habits in their life.

units.title: Learning from Legends: Tendulkar & Tata
units.topics: Students will learn from the inspirational lives of India's two legends, Sachin Tendulkar and Ratan Tata. They will implement these lessons through relatable case studies.

units.title: From House to Home: Listening & Understanding
units.topics: Active listening is an essential part of academic progress and communications. Students will learn to listen with their eyes, ears, mind, and heart.

units.title: Facing Failures: Welcoming Challenges
units.topics: This lecture enables students to revisit the way in which they approach challenges. Through the study of successful figures such as Disney, Lincoln and Bachchan, students will learn to face difficulties through a positive perspective.

units.title: Facing Failures: Significance of Failures
units.topics: Failure is a student’s daily source of fear, negativity, and depression. Students will be given the constructive skills to understand failure as formative learning experiences.

units.title: My India My Pride: Glorious Past - Part 1
units.topics: India’s ancient Rishis, scholars, and intellectuals have made tremendous contributions to the world, they developed an advanced, sophisticated culture and civilization which began thousands of years ago. Students will learn the importance of studying India’s glorious past so that they could develop a strong passion and pride for our nation.

units.title: My India My Pride: Glorious Past - Part 2
units.topics: Our ancient concepts can be used to seek revolutionary ideas and to generate inspiration. Students will develop a deeper interest in India’s Glorious Past – by appreciating the need to read about it, research it, write about it, and share it.

units.title: Learning from Legends: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
units.topics: Dr Kalam’s inspirational life displayed legendary qualities which apply to students (1) Dare to Dream (2) Work Hard (3) Get Good Guidance (4) Humility (5) Use Your Talents for the Benefit of Others

units.title: Soft Skills: Networking & Leadership
units.topics: Students are taught the means of building a professional network and developing a leadership attitude.

units.title: Soft Skills: Project Management
units.topics: Students will learn the secrets of project management through the Akshardham case study. They will then practice these skills through an activity relevant to student life.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Handling Social Media
units.topics: Students will learn how social media can become addictive and they will imbibe simple methods to take back control.

units.title: Facing Failures: Power of Faith
units.topics: Students will learn about the power and necessity of faith in our daily lives.

units.title: From House to Home: Bonding the Family
units.topics: Students will understand the importance of strong family relationships. They will learn how to overcome the generation gap and connect with their family more.

units.title: Selfless Service: Seva
units.topics: Students will learn that performing seva is beneficial to one’s health, wellbeing, and happiness. It also benefits and inspires others.

subjects.title: NSS (Theory & Practice) – III (Leadership, Personality Development and Disaster Management)

units.title: Leadership and Personality Development (Theory)
units.topics: 1. Leadership qualities and role of youth in nation building 2. Communication skills and teamwork 3. Ethical values, social responsibility, and citizenship 4. Time management, stress management, and life skills

units.title: Disaster Management and Special Camp Activities (Practical)
units.topics: (A) Disaster Management: 1. Types of disasters – Natural and Man-made 2. Disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response 3. Basic first aid and emergency handling. (B) NSS Special Camp / Field Activities: 1. Village adoption and rural development activities 2. Health camps, literacy drives, and awareness programmes 3. Documentation and reporting of NSS activities

files.title: CC251 3 Sports Proficiency and Participation (For sem IV)

subjects.title: Sports Proficiency and Participation in Sports Competitions (Inter-Collegiate Level)

units.title: Physical Fitness and Training Preparation
units.topics: Major components of physical fitness: Strength, Endurance, Flexibility, Speed, Agility, Balance, Coordination, Reaction Time, Body Composition, Daily exercise, practice matches, nutrition, rest and recovery.

units.title: Competitive Participation and Sports Proficiency
units.topics: Selection of individual or team sport, regular training under coaches/teachers, participation in inter-collegiate sports competitions, inter-zonal and inter-university sports competitions, sports proficiency and achievements.

files.title: CC251 5 Integrated Personality Development Programme II (For Sem IV)

subjects.title: Integrated Personality Development Program II

units.title: The Need for Values
units.topics: Students will learn about the need for values as part of their holistic development to become successful in their many roles - as ambitious students, reliable employees, caring family members, and considerate citizens.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Begin with the End in Mind
units.topics: Students will learn to visualize their future goals and will structure their lives through smart goals to give themselves direction and ultimately take them to where they want to go.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Being Addiction-Free
units.topics: Students will explore the detrimental effects of addictions on one's health, personal life, and family life. They will learn how to take control of their life by becoming addiction free.

units.title: Selfless Service: Case Study: Disaster Relief
units.topics: Students will apply previous lessons of seva, to analyse the case study of the Bhuj earthquake relief work.

units.title: Soft Skills: Teamwork & Harmony
units.topics: Students will learn the six steps of teamwork and harmony that are essential for students' professional and daily life.

units.title: My India My Pride: Present Scenario
units.topics: To implement the transformation of India from a developing country into a developed country it is necessary to have a value-based citizen. Students will see how the transformation to a greater India relies on the vision and efforts of themselves as a youth.

units.title: Learning from Legends: Leading Without Leading
units.topics: Students will explore a new approach to leadership, through humility.

units.title: My India My Pride: An Ideal Citizen – 1
units.topics: Students will learn that to become value-based citizens, they must first develop good values in their lives. They start by exploring the values of responsibility and integrity.

units.title: My India My Pride: An Ideal Citizen – 2
units.topics: Students will learn that by developing the values of loyalty, sincerity, and punctuality; they become indispensable and can leave a strong impression. They will start developing these values by trying to keep perfection in every small task and by looking at the bigger picture.

units.title: Facing Failures: Timeless Wisdom for Daily Life
units.topics: Students will learn the role wisdom plays in finding long-term stability. They will use ancient wisdom to solve their modern-day challenges.

units.title: From House to Home: Forgive & Forget
units.topics: Students will understand the importance and benefits that forgiveness plays in their personal and professional life. They will learn to apply this knowledge in realistic situations.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Stress Management
units.topics: Students will learn to cope with current and future causes of stress.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Better Health Better Future
units.topics: A healthy body prevents disease and stress; increases positivity, productivity, and brainpower. Students will learn to maintain good health through regular exercise, healthy eating habits, and regular and sufficient sleep.

units.title: Learning from Legends: Words of Wisdom
units.topics: A panel of learned and experienced mentors will personally answer practical questions that students face in their daily life.

units.title: Soft Skills: Financial Planning
units.topics: Students will develop a variety of practical financial skills that prepare them to become financially stable throughout their future careers.

units.title: Remaking Yourself: Impact of Company
units.topics: Students will understand that the type of company that we keep, has a crucial role in determining who we are and who we will become. They will develop the ability to create a positive environment around them.

units.title: Life After IPDC
units.topics: This concluding lecture encourages students to keep practicing these priceless lessons and prepares them for the next steps in their lives.

files.title: Sem-1 Course Entrepreneurship Essentials

subjects.title: ENTREPRENEURSHIP ESSENTIALS - I

units.title: Entrepreneurship Fundamentals & Context
units.topics: Meaning and concept, attributes and mind-set of entrepreneurial and intrapreneurial leadership, role models in each and their role in economic development. An understanding of how to build entrepreneurial mind-set, skillsets, attributes and networks while on campus. Core Teaching Tool : Simulation, Game, Industry Case Studies (Personalized for students – 16 industries to choose from), Venture Activity

units.title: Problem & Customer Identification
units.topics: Understanding and analysing the macro-Problem and Industry perspective, technological, socio economic and urbanization trends and their implication on new opportunities. Identifying passion, identifying and defining problem using Design thinking principles. Analysing problem and validating with the potential customer. Iterating problem-customer fit. Understanding customer segmentation, creating and validating customer personas. Competition and Industry trends mapping and assessing initial opportunity. Core Teaching Tool : Several types of activities including Class, game, Gen AI, ‘Get out of the Building’ and Venture Activity

units.title: Solution design, Prototyping & Opportunity Assessment and Sizing
units.topics: Understanding Customer Jobs-to-be-done and crafting innovative solution design to map to customer’s needs and create a strong value proposition. Developing Problem-solution fit in an iterative manner. Understanding prototyping and MVP. Developing a feasibility prototype with differentiating value, features and benefits. Initial testing for proof -of-concept and iterate on the prototype. Assess relative market position via competition analysis, sizing the market and assess scope and potential scale of the opportunity. Core Teaching Tool: Venture Activity, no-code Innovation tools, Class activity
